CHAPTER 1
This book argues that teams can reduce customer churn by treating onboarding as a measurable learning loop. The first principle is simple: every handoff should produce evidence. For example, a weekly survey can reveal where customers lose confidence before renewal.

Research from subscription companies shows that unclear first-week milestones predict later churn. The framework in this chapter asks leaders to map promise, proof, and reinforcement for each onboarding step.

CHAPTER 2
The second principle is to turn support requests into product signals. You will improve retention when each recurring question is tagged, grouped, and reviewed with product and success leaders. A case study from a B2B platform showed a 14 percent retention lift after teams fixed the top three recurring setup blockers.

This method can work quickly, but it fails when leaders promise certainty without evidence. By the end of the book, you will have a repeatable system for measuring trust, friction, and renewal risk.
